question: What result follows for the adept when the prescribed act has been completed?
premises: The act is described as having been done.
The adept is the subject of the result.
The adept becomes a vessel for supreme accomplishment.
inference: Upon completion of the prescribed act, the adept becomes fit for supreme accomplishment.
uncertainties: arthaḥ may serve as a concluding gloss rather than part of the main predication.
plain_english: When this is done, the adept becomes a vessel for supreme accomplishment; that is the meaning.
